title: Small cellular slices compatible with a prescribed diagram slice
statement:
Work in a fixed universe. Let $\kappa$ be uncountable regular and $\mathcal A$ an ordinary locally $\kappa$-presentable category with small Hom sets. Here locally $\kappa$-presentable means having all small colimits [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit] and being generated under small $\kappa$-filtered colimits by a small family of objects whose Hom functors preserve those colimits; regular and $\kappa$-filtered have their union and cocone meanings. Let $D$ be an ordinary category with fewer than $\kappa$ morphisms. Let $f:F\to G$ be a natural transformation of $D$-diagrams in $\mathcal A$. For each $d$, fix a $\kappa$-good $L$-cellular tree with root $F(d)$ and colimit $G(d)$ realizing $f(d)$, with small well-founded indexing poset $T_d$, as in [def-coef-good-cellular-tree]. The attaching arrows of the class $L$ have $\kappa$-presentable endpoints. Write $Y_d(B)$ for its colimit on a downward-closed subset $B\subseteq T_d$, taken in $F(d)/\mathcal A$.

A slice consists of downward-closed subsets $B_d\subseteq T_d$ and maps $Y_d(B_d)\to Y_e(B_e)$ for every arrow $d\to e$ of $D$, making $d\mapsto Y_d(B_d)$ a functor and $F\to Y(B)\to G$ natural transformations whose composite is $f$. An extension of slices means inclusions of their subsets for which the canonical tree-colimit maps form a natural transformation. Given any slice $M$ with subsets $A_d$ (not assumed small in cardinality) and subsets $E_d\subseteq T_d$ with $|E_d|<\kappa$, there exist slices $N,N'$ with subsets $B_d$ and $B_d\cap A_d$, respectively, such that $E_d\subseteq B_d$, $|B_d|<\kappa$, and $N'$ extends to both $N$ and $M$. Thus the canonical maps from the intersection colimits to the two slice colimits are natural. The root and the colimits $F(d),G(d),Y_d(A_d)$ need not be $\kappa$-presentable.
